question.text: A non-resident corporate LP in Nilgiri Multi-Strategy Fund receives interest income of INR 1 crore (coupon from debenture holdings via the fund). Assuming no beneficial treaty rate applies and using the workbook's effective rate of 38.22% for foreign corporate investors on interest income, the tax liability is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Workbook: 'Any income in the nature of interest income would be subject to tax at the rate of ... 38.22% (in the hands of foreign corporate investors, subject to beneficial tax rate under the relevant Tax Treaty).' Tax = 1,00,00,000 × 38.22% = INR 38,22,000 = INR 38.22 lakh. The Trap: INR 42.74 lakh applies the individual/AOP MMR (wrong assessee class). INR 34.944 lakh uses the domestic corporate rate. INR 20 lakh uses a generic 20% under Section 115A that ignores surcharge and cess. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D drills the same rate table on Cat I/II NR investors. XIX-C covers both. XIX-E tests it specifically where the Cat III fund, having no pass-through, pays upfront at fund level (and may offer treaty credit certificate). Manager's Pro-Tip: For treaty-resident NR LPs, collect the TRC + Form 10F upfront so Nilgiri can apply the DTAA rate (often 10%-15% on interest) instead of 38.22%. Without documentation, the fund is bound to withhold at the ITA rate and the LP must chase refund — a painful friction, particularly for Singapore/Mauritius/Netherlands LPs.
